conventions.convention: A finite quartic graph has a nonempty finite vertex set, connected internal multigraph, and exactly four incidence slots per vertex. Internal edges consume two distinct slots, including loops; external half-edges consume one. Parallel edges remain distinct.

D is a positive integer; L := I−V+1. Each formal loop integration contributes degree D, each internal scalar propagator contributes −2, and each quartic vertex contributes zero. The superficial degree is ω_D := DL−2I; zero is called logarithmic superficial degree without asserting convergence or divergence.

Formal natural-unit mass degrees use ℏ=c=1, coordinate degree −1, derivative degree 1, measure degree −D, and degree zero for both displayed action terms. Dilation is φ_b(x)=b^{−(D−2)/2}φ(x/b), b>0. Relevant, marginal, and irrelevant mean positive, zero, and negative monomial dilation exponent respectively.

The distribution-extension calculation is separate from graph counting, assumes AC, and uses the exact current draft scale-anomaly statement conditionally. Its kernel is 1/(16π⁴|x|⁴), with smooth compact cutoff equal to one near zero and positive scales μ,ν.

load_bearing.statement: The attachment map from internal-edge ends and external half-edges to the four slots at every vertex is a bijection. Define L := I−V+1 and ω_D(Γ) := DL−2I. By convention, ω_D(Γ)=0 is called a logarithmic superficial degree.

For D∈ℤ≥1 and a finite quartic graph, 4V=2I+E and L=I−V+1. Its superficial degree is ω_D(Γ)=DL−2I=D+(D−4)V−(D−2)E/2. In D=4 this reduces to ω₄(Γ)=4−E. These identities do not assert convergence or divergence of an actual graph integral.

For D∈ℤ≥1, φ∈C_c^∞(ℝ^D;ℝ), integer r≥3, and real g_r≠0, under the specified dimensionless-action mass-degree convention, [φ]=(D−2)/2 and [g_r]=D−r(D−2)/2. For b>0, S_kin(φ_b)=S_kin(φ) and S_r(φ_b)=b^{D−r(D−2)/2}S_r(φ). A quartic monomial has exponent 4−D.

published_dependencies.used_for: The graph definition's loop, parallel-edge, and underlying-simple-graph connectivity conventions, including connectedness of a single vertex.
The example's explicitly adopted AC premise for its separate conditional distribution-extension calculation.

alerts.finding: Proof step 2.2 says, “Apply [F7] separately to its positive and negative parts.” The Statement permits any χ∈D(ℝ⁴) equal to one near zero; def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set defines D using complex-valued functions. Thus χ(μx)−χ(νx) may be complex-valued and has no positive and negative parts. The argument needs the componentwise real/imaginary application of the nonnegative polar formula. The identity itself survives this immediate justification.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite supplies distribution scaling and extension context; the graph-count and engineering-dilation results do not identify superficial degree with distribution scaling degree. The companion example faithfully instantiates the exact four-dimensional kernel, cutoff and positive-scale hypotheses, retains AC and conditional draft status, and reproduces the scale-change coefficient and absence of a same-degree homogeneous extension. Neither page identifies this calculation with a graph amplitude or physical running coupling.
